Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

simply adverb

plainly, in plain words

also to put it simply, plainly, in plain words, frankly, talk turkey, speak plainly

classical

Cic. Off. 2.31: sī est simpliciter breviterque dīcendum
Cael. in Cic. Fam. 8.6.1: simpliciter et candidē
Traupman 379

simpliciter

adverb · Wiktionary

simply, plainly; frankly

Without art or ornament, or without holding anything back (Lewis & Short: “simply, plainly, straightforwardly … frankly, candidly”).

Other words

  • plānē — plainly, clearly, so as to be understood

    adverb · also used · classical · Cic. Phil. 7.17: quī plānē et Latīnē loquuntur; Cic. de Or. 2.303: ut plānius dīcam · Wiktionary

    “To put it more simply” is ut plānius dīcam. For “simply” meaning “absolutely” (simply impossible), see quite.

  • Latīnē loquī — speak plainly, say it in plain words

    also used · classical · Cic. Phil. 7.17: quī plānē et Latīnē loquuntur; Traupman 110: Latīnē loquī cum (+ ablative)

    Plain Latin is plain speech: sī Latīnē loquī volumus, if we are to use words properly (Cic. Caecin. 21, Lewis & Short s.v. armō).

Examples

  • Haec autem, sī est simpliciter breviterque dīcendum, quibus rēbus pariuntur ā singulīs, eīsdem ferē ā multitūdine.

    To put it simply and briefly, these are won from the many by much the same means as from one person.Cic. Off. 2.31

  • solēre mē cēdere et, ut plānius dīcam, fugere

    that I usually give ground, or, to put it more plainly, run awayCic. de Or. 2.303

See also only, quite.
